AUTHOR: Saleh
TITLE: A realistic fish-habitat dataset to evaluate algorithms for underwater visual analysis
REGION: Hinchinbrook/Palm Islands region, North Queensland, Australia; some from Western Australia
SPECIES: Fish (no species labels); juvenile fish communities of 20 tropical coastal habitats
DATA: DeepFish (own footage from Bradley et al. 2019): 39,766 frames (FishClf), 3,200 point-annotated (FishLoc), 620 segmentation-annotated (FishSeg)
V_EV: Data collection: 'Video recording were carried out during daylight hours, and in relatively low turbidity periods.' Turbidity not measured; low-turbidity periods selected without characterisation; no results stratified by visibility.
D2: 50/20/30 per habitat, balanced foreground/background (FishClf 19,883/7,953/11,930; FishLoc 1,600/640/960; FishSeg 310/124/186)
D_EV: Dataset splits: 'We randomly select 50% training, 20% for validation and 30% for testing for each habitat while ensuring that the number of background and foreground images are equal'
R_EV: Table 3: all tasks 'evaluated on the FishClf dataset, counting and localization on the FishLoc dataset, and segmentation on the FishSeg dataset' — held-out splits of the same dataset only.
C_EV: Localization results: 'the predicted probability map are thresholded to become 1 if they are larger than 0.5 and 0 otherwise' — fixed default threshold; no false-positive or uncertainty analysis of outputs.
E_EV: Counting results: 'Ci is the true fish count for image i and Ĉi is the model's predicted fish count' — MAE 0.38 vs point-annotation counts of the same images (Table 3).
ARCH: ResNet-50 backbone + feed-forward head (classification, regression counting); FCN8 upsampling path with LCFCN loss (localization/counting); FCN8 with focal loss (segmentation)
NOTE: Benchmark/dataset paper. V_ALL: both the P clause (V1=정성 서술만, 'relatively low turbidity periods') and the N clause (footage deliberately restricted to low-turbidity periods without characterising it) apply; N chosen as the more specific rule — verifier may prefer P. V3=Y only for 'daylight hours'; depth was measured by acoustic sounder but no values are reported (V2=NR). Split is random per image stratified by habitat and fg/bg (the canonical DeepFish 50/20/30 split); frames from the same video can fall in different splits, no duplicate handling or leakage discussion → D_ALL=N. E1=사람 계수와 비교 is a borderline call: per-image count MAE against human point annotations of the same images is a counting benchmark rather than an ecological estimate; a stricter reading gives E1=없음/E_ALL=N. Segmentation is motivated by size/weight estimation but no length/biomass is actually estimated. Dataset and code public (alzayats.github.io/DeepFish).
